bull.b: The sharp revenue rebound and improving gross margin indicate stronger business activity and better unit economics. If sustained, this recovery could provide operating leverage and improve the company’s ability to move toward durable profitability.

A shift from heavy cash burn to positive operating cash flow and marginally positive free cash flow is a constructive fundamental inflection. It reduces immediate reliance on external funding, although the small cushion still requires further proof of consistency.

The latest reported quarter points to broadening operational improvement rather than revenue growth alone, with better gross profit and a return to modest operating profit. Higher cash and equity could strengthen capacity to fund operations and expansion.

bear.b: Despite the revenue rebound, the company remains loss-making and only marginally profitable before depreciation, interest, and taxes. Continued low operating profitability leaves limited protection against cost pressure and makes the recovery vulnerable to another downturn.

Debt remains slightly above equity, constraining financial flexibility even after improvement from 2025. Elevated leverage increases sensitivity to weaker margins, working-capital needs, or refinancing pressure and may limit investment capacity in a cyclical steel business.

The equity-raising facility provides liquidity but creates a potential source of shareholder dilution if shares are issued. Its availability also signals that external capital may remain relevant while profitability and free-cash-flow generation are not yet robust.
